content.overview: Cultivation records must be trustworthy enough to reconstruct what happened. This lesson applies established data-integrity concepts to routine cultivation documentation without presenting pharmaceutical guidance as cannabis law.

vocabulary.definition: Recorded at the time the activity or observation occurs, or under a controlled process that preserves the true timing.
Linked clearly to the person or system that created or changed the record.
The degree to which records remain complete, consistent, accurate, attributable and reconstructable across their lifecycle.

sections.title: Record facts when they happen
sections.body: MHRA data-integrity guidance describes data as attributable, legible and permanent, contemporaneous, original and accurate, with completeness, consistency, endurance and availability across the lifecycle. This course transfers those quality principles to cultivation records; it does not claim MHRA rules govern U.S. cannabis operations.

sections.title: Corrections preserve history
sections.body: Paper or digital corrections follow the facility's controlled method so the original entry and change history are not concealed. Missing data remain identified as missing rather than guessed, and measurements include enough context such as unit, sample or plant identity, location and time to remain meaningful.

workedExamples: A measurement is corrected without erasing the original value, following the supplied correction procedure.
A pH or EC value is recorded with the measurement type, unit, sample identity and time rather than as a context-free number.
commonMistakes: Backfilling observations from memory as if they were recorded live.
Overwriting an original value without preserving the correction history.
content.practicalApplication: Correct a set of flawed cultivation records containing missing units, ambiguous identity, late entries, overwritten values and guessed data.
content.summary: Trustworthy records are factual, attributable, timely and reconstructable. Technicians preserve correction history, include necessary context and never invent missing data.

blocks.title: A record is useful only if another person can trust and reconstruct it
blocks.body: This course transfers established data-integrity principles to routine cultivation documentation: make the record attributable, legible, timely, accurate, complete enough for its purpose, and durable enough to reconstruct the event. That is a quality principle for this curriculum; it is not a claim that MHRA pharmaceutical rules govern U.S. cannabis operations.

blocks.title: Record-quality questions
rows: Person or system is attributable under the controlled method
Anonymous or shared identity with no reliable attribution
Timing reflects the real activity or a controlled late-entry process
Backfilled from memory as though recorded live
What exactly was measured or observed?
Identity, location, measurement type, unit, and context are present where needed
Original entry/change history remains visible under the facility method
Missing data or incomplete work is identified honestly
Guessed values inserted to make the record look complete

left.label: Controlled correction
left.body: An incorrect value is corrected using the facility method so the original value, corrected value, identity of the change, timing, and required reason remain reconstructable.

right.label: Silent overwrite
right.body: The original entry is erased or replaced so the record appears to have always contained the corrected value, hiding what actually happened.

blocks.title: A measurement was missed one hour ago
blocks.setting: A required measurement was not recorded during the task. The technician now remembers approximately what the display showed but did not write it down or save a system record.
options: Enter the remembered value with the original time so the record looks complete
Enter an average value from nearby readings
Follow the facility's missing-data or late-entry process and do not represent a guess as contemporaneous measurement data
Leave the entire record blank with no explanation
blocks.answer: Follow the facility's missing-data or late-entry process and do not represent a guess as contemporaneous measurement data.
blocks.feedback: A remembered estimate is not equivalent to a measurement record captured at the time. The record should preserve the missing or late status honestly.

blocks.title: Context-rich cultivation record example
blocks.description: A measurement becomes more useful when enough context is present to understand what was measured, where, when, and by whom.

fields.label: Measurement / observation
fields.value: Specify pH, EC, temperature, count, condition, or other defined observation

fields.label: Value / result
fields.value: Actual result with the correct unit or status where applicable

fields.label: Material / sample / asset identity
fields.value: Controlled identifier that ties the record to the correct object

fields.label: Location
fields.value: Room, zone, reservoir, work area, or other required location

fields.label: Time
fields.value: When the observation or activity occurred

fields.label: Attribution
fields.value: Person or system responsible for the entry

fields.label: Correction history
fields.value: Preserved using the facility's controlled method when a change is needed

blocks.note: The exact record fields depend on the task and facility process; the principle is that the data remain meaningful and reconstructable.

blocks.title: Repair a flawed record set without erasing history
blocks.instructions: Audit a packet containing missing units, ambiguous identities, late entries, overwritten values, guessed data, and one legitimate correction.
prompts: Identify which entries cannot be interpreted without more context.
Separate missing data from incorrect data.
Apply the supplied correction method while preserving the original entry.
Flag every guessed value that is represented as fact.
Explain what the next shift can and cannot reconstruct from the corrected packet.
blocks.artifact: Corrected record set and data-integrity audit

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: The goal is not perfect-looking paperwork. The goal is a trustworthy record of reality. Preserve timing, identity, context, correction history, and missing information so another qualified person can reconstruct what actually occurred.
